key_insight: Microscopic impurities seed perovskite degradation, and machine learning-supported optical imaging can flag these harmful defects within seconds.
engineering_relevance: Rapid, non-invasive impurity screening could help manufacturers assess film stability before device fabrication and support scalable perovskite solar cell production.
method: Identify impurities using nano-FTIR spectroscopy and high-resolution optical and scanning probe techniques.
Use photo-stress experiments to locate degradation initiation sites.
Detect and quantify impurities with reflected-light microscopy and machine learning-supported image analysis.
evidence_signal: Photo-stress experiments showed degradation initiating at impurity–perovskite interfaces, while higher impurity density was associated with faster early degradation.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative detection accuracy or validation across different film compositions and manufacturing conditions.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
